text: Why does Benny pay sixty-six dollars to fill his tank...
when in Iran, a full tank costs less than a pack of gum?
Okay. I'm going to Iran.
One last fill-up before the trip. Four forty-one a gallon.
Sixty-six bucks! For liquid dinosaurs!
Tehran. First gas station. Fifteen hundred tomans a liter.
Is that... a lot?
Less than three cents a gallon.
I've lost more than that in my couch!
Catch: that's for locals with a fuel card. First sixty liters a month.
After that? Up to ten thousand tomans.
Still pocket change!
So who's actually paying for this?
One: the government sells fuel below cost.
Two: the money. On the street, one dollar buys over two million rials.
So the gas is cheap... because the money is broken?
Pretty much. And America? Oil sells at world prices. Plus refining, trucks, and taxes.
Final twist: Benny's sixty-six bucks? Over a hundred and forty million rials.
I'm a millionaire!
In Tehran. In Texas, he's just a guy with an empty tank.
Expensive gas, or cheap gas with broken money? Which is worse? Comment below.
